events.description: An authorized S3 team member executed a command intended to remove a small number of servers for an S3 billing-related subsystem, but an input was entered incorrectly and a larger set of servers was removed than intended.
The removed servers supported the index subsystem and the placement subsystem, causing both to require a full restart and making S3 unable to service requests.
Other AWS services in US-EAST-1 relying on S3 were impacted, including the S3 console, EC2 new instance launches, EBS volumes needing S3 snapshot data, and AWS Lambda.

The team could not update individual service status on the AWS Service Health Dashboard due to its dependency on Amazon S3; status was communicated via the AWS Twitter feed and SHD banner text instead.
The team was able to update individual services' status on the AWS Service Health Dashboard again.
The index subsystem activated enough capacity to begin servicing S3 GET, LIST, and DELETE requests.
The index subsystem was fully recovered and GET, LIST, and DELETE APIs were functioning normally.

events.time: February 28, 2017, after index subsystem recovery (before 1:54PM PST)
events.description: The placement subsystem began recovery once the index subsystem was functional.
The placement subsystem finished recovery and S3 was operating normally.
Other impacted AWS services began recovering, with some requiring additional time to process accumulated backlogs.
